variables.name: control_subgroup
variables.original: Sample ID prefix of the healthy dogs (H1-8, HI1-8)

cleaning_notes: Cytokine sheet: sample IDs with an inner space were joined to the haematology IDs: 'BK 1' -> 'BK1'.

Source: S1 Table workbook (sheets CYTOKINES, HEMATOLOGY; the third sheet 'Hoja1' is empty). Both sheets were joined on the original sample ID and the block (healthy, diseased day 1, diseased day 7); every sample is in both sheets.

Long format: one record per dog and day. Infected dogs: timepoint day_1 (admission) and day_7 (6 days after imidocarb), numeric day 1 and 7. Healthy controls: one record, timepoint 'single', day null.

Day of the cytokine blocks: the record and data.md say the two 'Diseased' blocks of the CYTOKINES sheet (31 and 30 rows) have no day label. They do: the label cells read 'Diseased                day 1' and 'Diseased                 day 7'; the day text sits after a run of spaces and is hidden in a narrow column. The blocks were assigned from these labels. Independent support: (a) the only ID in the day-1 block and not in the day-7 block is BK11, the same dog that is the only one missing from the haematology 'Diseased day 7' block (the article reports one death and n = 30 on day 7); (b) the medians of each block reproduce the article's Table 2 day-1 and day-7 medians for all 9 cytokines (checks file); (c) IL-10 is at its floor in 1 of 31 day-1 and 28 of 30 day-7 samples, matching the reported day-7 IL-10 median of 1 pg/mL.
Haematology day labels come from the text rows 'Diseased day 1' and 'Diseased day 7' of the HEMATOLOGY sheet.

Neutral dog_id: the original IDs (H*, HI*, B*, BK*) carry the label (B = uncomplicated, BK = complicated, per the side legend of the CYTOKINES sheet). They are replaced by salted-hash IDs; the original ID is only in the outcomes file.

Blood for cytokines was taken 6-8 h after imidocarb dipropionate (6 mg/kg SC on day 1) per the article, so day-1 values are early post-treatment, not pre-treatment. All infected dogs also had supportive care (fluids, anti-inflammatories, transfusion if haematocrit < 20%) that the file does not record.

Healthy controls: 8 'H' and 8 'HI' dogs. control_subgroup keeps this prefix. The article describes two control subgroups of 8: dogs given prophylactic imidocarb (group 2a) and dogs at routine visits (group 2b). Reading HI as the imidocarb subgroup is an inference from the prefix; the file does not say so. The article says group 2a was sampled at admission and 6 days later, but the file has one sample per control dog; which time point it is, is not stated.

Assay floors (per the record, confirmed as the minimum value in the file): IL-10 0.8, IL-18 2, IL-2 10, IL-15 12, IL-8 10 pg/mL. Values at the floor are kept and flagged 'floor' in censored. Counts over all 77 samples: il10 45, il18 18, il2 1, il15 3, il8 1. Observed minima of all cytokines: gmcsf 59.7, kc 27.6, il2 10.0, il7 31.3, il8 10.0, il10 0.8, il15 12.0, il18 2.0, mcp1 155.8. Values below a floor: none.

FLAG: the IL-2 floor of 10 occurs once (one control sample); the next-lowest IL-2 value 12.1 is frequent and may also be a floor-like interpolated value. Only the record's floors were flagged. Cytokine values are heavily quantised (repeated values such as IL-18 83, 144.9, 188.4); kept as reported.

FLAG: the CYTOKINES sheet has an unlabelled column with the word 'Dead' beside 9 complicated dogs in the first block and 8 in the second. The article reports one death. The column is not used as an outcome and nothing from it is in the features or outcomes file.

Haematology units are not in the headers. They follow the reference-range block of the sheet: counts 10^9/L, erythrocytes 10^12/L, HMT %, differentials %. HMT was converted from % to L/L (/100). No other unit was changed.
The reference-range block of the HEMATOLOGY sheet (haematology and biochemistry ranges, with no data) was not read.

The file has no haemoglobin, red cell indices, parasitaemia, biochemistry, CRP, clinical signs, age, sex or breed. The article gives sex only as group totals (complicated 8 female, 10 male; uncomplicated 5 female, 8 male).
Haematology consistency checks (count against % x WBC, total granulocytes against segmented + band %, MCV implied by HMT / erythrocytes). Values are kept as reported; each failure is a FLAG below.
FLAG: S-CB017:d003 day 1: mono 2.3 vs mono_pct 27.0% of WBC 19.0 = 5.13
FLAG: S-CB017:d008 day 1: hct 35.0% and rbc 35.0 give MCV 10 fL (implausible; rbc is probably the haematocrit typed twice)
FLAG: S-CB017:d038 day 7: neut_band 0.7 vs neut_band_pct 1.0% of WBC 6.8 = 0.07
FLAG: S-CB017:d038 day 7: neut_seg 42.0 vs neut_seg_pct 62.0% of WBC 6.8 = 4.22
FLAG: S-CB017:d047 day 7: neut_seg 1.4 vs neut_seg_pct 59.0% of WBC 28.3 = 16.7
FLAG: S-CB017:d043 control: mono 0.8 vs mono_pct 1.0% of WBC 12.6 = 0.13
FLAG: S-CB017:d043 control: eos 1.6 vs eos_pct 3.0% of WBC 12.6 = 0.38
FLAG: S-CB017:d004 control: mono 0.0 vs mono_pct 4.0% of WBC 13.1 = 0.52

The n:l ratio equals Total gran % / Lymph % or (segmented + band) / lymphocyte counts (within 5% or 0.15) in 75 of 77 samples, so a high n:l (for example 99) follows the reported percentages and is not flagged on its own. FLAG: exceptions: S-CB017:d015 day 1: nl_ratio 4.6 vs gran % / lymph % = 4.9 and (seg + band) / lymph counts = 5.1; S-CB017:d008 day 7: nl_ratio 2.6 vs gran % / lymph % = 4.0 and (seg + band) / lymph counts = 4.0.
Floating-point noise in the cells was rounded to 10 decimals.
